exam.title: RRB Officer Scale-I - Inequality Topic Test 01

questions.question: Statement: A > B >= C = D. Conclusions: I. A > D. II. B > D.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: A > B >= C = D guarantees A > D. B may equal D, so B > D is not definite.

questions.question: Statement: P <= Q < R <= S. Conclusions: I. P < R. II. S > Q.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: The strict Q < R link makes P < R and S > Q definite.

questions.question: Statement: M = N >= O > P. Conclusions: I. M > P. II. O < M.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: M = N >= O > P guarantees M > P. O may equal M, so O < M is not definite.

questions.question: Statement: X < Y <= Z. Conclusions: I. Z > X. II. X = Z.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: X < Y <= Z guarantees Z > X, making equality between X and Z impossible.

questions.question: Statement: A >= B >= C. Conclusions: I. A >= C. II. C > A.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: A is at least as large as C. Therefore C cannot be greater than A.

questions.question: Statement: J < K = L <= M. Conclusions: I. J < L. II. M >= K.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: K = L makes J < L definite, and L <= M makes M >= K definite.

questions.question: Statements: R > S; T >= R. Conclusions: I. T > S. II. S < T.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: T >= R > S guarantees T > S. Both conclusions express that same relationship.

questions.question: Statements: U <= V; W < V. Conclusions: I. U < W. II. U >= W.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: U and W cannot be compared from the statements, but U < W and U >= W are complementary and exhaustive.

questions.question: Statement: H = I < J <= K. Conclusions: I. H < K. II. K > I.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: H = I < J <= K guarantees H < K and K > I.

questions.question: Statements: A > B; C > B. Conclusions: I. A > C. II. C > A.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: A and C are separate branches above B. They may also be equal, so neither strict conclusion is definite and the pair is not exhaustive.

questions.question: Statement: F >= G > H = I. Conclusions: I. I < F. II. G > I.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: F >= G > H = I guarantees F > I and G > I.

questions.question: Statement: L < M <= N < O. Conclusions: I. L < N. II. O > M.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: Both conclusions follow directly from the connected increasing chain.

questions.question: Statement: P = Q <= R < S. Conclusions: I. P < S. II. R > Q.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: P = Q <= R < S guarantees P < S. R may equal Q, so R > Q is not definite.

questions.question: Statement: A < B = C > D. Conclusions: I. A < D. II. C > A.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: A and D cannot be compared because both are below B=C. C > A follows directly.

questions.question: Statement: W <= X = Y < Z. Conclusions: I. W < Z. II. Z > X.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: W <= X = Y < Z guarantees W < Z and Z > X.

questions.question: Codes: P @ Q means P > Q; P # Q means P <= Q; P $ Q means P = Q. Statement: A # B @ C $ D. Conclusions: I. B > D. II. A < D.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: Decoded: A <= B > C = D. Therefore B > D, while A and D cannot be compared.

questions.question: Codes: P % Q means P >= Q; P & Q means P < Q; P * Q means P = Q. Statement: P % Q & R * S. Conclusions: I. P < S. II. S > Q.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: Decoded: P >= Q < R = S. S > Q is definite, while P and S cannot be compared.

questions.question: Statements: E > F >= G; H < G. Conclusions: I. E > H. II. F > H.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: Combining the statements gives E > F >= G > H, so both conclusions follow.

questions.question: Statements: T <= U; U <= V. Conclusions: I. T = V. II. V >= T.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: T <= U <= V guarantees V >= T, but equality between T and V is only possible, not definite.

questions.question: Statement: C > D < E. Conclusions: I. C > E. II. C <= E.

options.E: Either Conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: C and E cannot be compared from the statement, while C > E and C <= E are complementary and exhaustive.
